chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ja'far and Salih ibn Khalid from Abu Jamilah from Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
About a house that one buys, in which there is an addition of the road (easement), he said: 'If that was included in what was specified for him, then there is no objection to it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy a house if the road included in the deed is larger than usual?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition for validity in property sales involving incidental road access, ruling that if the extra path falls within the defined boundaries of the sold plot, it is free from *gharar* (uncertainty). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor ambiguities in physical boundaries do not invalidate a contract when the core subject matter is clearly identified and accessible. It highlights the practical application of *gharar* in real estate transactions, emphasizing clarity of ownership over rigid geometric standardization.
